I have spent 17hrs so far playing this game and really enjoying it. Its super easy to hop in and do a few quick runs if you are short on time, or if you are free for a bit you can spend much longer inside the maps looting and engaging with enemies.

There are a TON of quests to do and give you purpose to go back in and work on tasks. There is a great deal of stations to craft and upgrade in your hideout as well. The amount of items you can collect, weapons, equipment, etc... They definitely filled the game up.

Right now I only have access to 3 maps, the first one, by now is pretty simple, but I still go back into it for quests and if I need some easy runs to save up some money. The 2nd map is bigger and poses more of a threat, the 3rd being the biggest that I haven't fully explored yet but again poses a bigger threat as well.

There are bosses to fight and find in the game, hidden areas etc.
Not to mention the blatant and most obvious about the game, being heavily influenced by EFT. Its pretty funny the things that you will see that remind you or are taken right from EFT. You can tell that the team is passionate about that game but wanted to give their own take on it.

Also its Ducks... Its super cute and silly.

Something I would like to see is maybe some more maps, seems like there will be more available to me at a later time, I just have not found them yet.

I really suggest giving this game a shot, it's great fun.
And I don't write reviews often, but felt this one deserved it.

Escape From Annoying Ducking Missions

This game has a solid foundation, and I can tell that’s a big reason people have reacted strongly to it. The ducks, the 2.5D graphics — all of that is great. It’s fun to run around and play in this world. But once you’ve played for more than 10 hours, you start to feel the game’s deeper problems.

My main frustration is the mission structure, which is just super annoying. For example, missions often force you to use the weapon they want you to use instead of the one you prefer. What does it matter if I use one rifle over another — or if I want to use a pistol for fun? The game frequently includes anti-fun mission design that stifles creativity or prevents you from experimenting with different methods (like using a bear trap, for instance).

Another major annoyance is the mission pathing structure, which is incredibly aggravating. It’s like all the worst parts of traveling through an airport — multiple stops, endless backtracking — but imagine doing that while juggling several passports at once. Just truly awful.

If this game were in Early Access, I could understand some of this. But it’s not, and it feels like it never went through the refinement and feedback needed to smooth out these terrible missions. The challenge should come from navigating the dangers of the environment, not from tedious back-and-forth busywork.

The game also does a terrible job of explaining what items are important and what’s just vendor trash. There’s little guidance to help you set yourself up properly. Often it’s the small, easy-to-overlook items that end up being critical — like the cup item, which many players wouldn’t think to pick up. Even when you can craft things, it’s easy to forget with the sheer number of items and menus in this game’s awful UI system. And seriously — why can’t I sort items by anything in a 2025 game? That’s just unforgivable.

The combat is fun but becomes repetitive quickly, since there’s not much depth to it. You can use the same strategy against most enemies as long as your gear is decent. In Zero Sievert, this was handled much better — that game had more interesting combat methods and far more diverse biomes. I was really disappointed to find this game mostly limited to forests and labs — that’s it.

Overall, even though this game is fairly priced and has some fun moments, I can’t overlook the massive number of annoyances that could have been easily fixed. These games are meant to encourage you to play on the hardest difficulty — but why would you, when all these frustrating elements are piled on top? This isn’t an evolution of the genre; Zero Sievert handled it much better.

It’s a damn shame, because this genre deserves more good games. Maybe if this had co-op, it could have been better — but it doesn’t, so what have we really achieved here? I feel like buying this game just means repeating Zero Sievert in a more annoying form — as a funny-looking duck. And honestly, most of the time you barely even see the duck since he’s covered in armor. Maybe they should’ve gone with multiple animal types instead.

Ultimately, I can’t recommend this game unless it gets at least a year’s worth of serious patching.

A very well-made top-down/isometric (you can change the camera angle with Y) extraction shooter. Took me around 85 hours to reach the end, enjoyed the whole process. Did I mention it has Steam Workshop support with a bustilng mod community?

Difficulty can be changed at any time and there is no Achievement tied to it, so there's no downside. The one exception is the Custom difficulty where you can adjust certain parameters, but Achievements are disabled and you can't change to/from it.

If you're fine with the art direction (ducks!), this will scratch that "extraction shooter but fun" itch with excellence. Highly recommended.

Duckov is a top down extraction shooter developed by a team with their wing on the pulse. They know exactly what makes their game fun, and the parody is absolutely on point if you've played any Tarkov at all. The game manages to nail all the excitement and challenge of a looter shooter along with satisfying meta progression. It allows pausing, and loads very quickly between runs. The mod support is also fantastic and I suggest checking out the workshop once you have a few hours under your belt.

I highly suggest picking this up.
